message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to current air‑quality data, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment. However, here’s what you can do to find up‑to‑date information:

| Source | How to Use |
|--------|------------|
| **AirNow.gov** | Enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code to see the latest AQI, pollutant levels (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO, SO₂), and health recommendations. |
| **AQICN.org** | Search for “Los Angeles” or use the mobile app. It shows a color‑coded map, hourly forecasts, and historical trends. |
| **Local news sites** | Many local stations publish live air‑quality dashboards on their websites. |
| **Mobile apps** | Apps like “Plume Labs: Air Report” or “EPA AirNow” give push notifications when AQI changes. |

If you’re planning outdoor activities, check the AQI today and tomorrow. A value below 50 is considered good; 51–100 is moderate; 101–150 is unhealthy for sensitive groups; 151–200 is unhealthy; 201–300 is very unhealthy; and 301+ is hazardous.

Let me know if you’d like a quick summary of typical Los Angeles AQI ranges for different seasons or how weather patterns affect it!
